articles.body: Google Hotels is one of the best places to compare hotel prices: for every hotel it shows the rate on Booking.com, Expedia, Agoda, Hotels.com, the hotel's own website and a dozen smaller sites, for the exact dates you pick. There is no official API for it, though. I needed this data for a price-monitoring project, so I built three scrapers for it and published them on Apify. This post shows how to use them from Python. Disclosure: I'm the author of these scrapers, and they are paid per result. New Apify accounts get free monthly credit, which covers a few thousand hotels. All code is in this repo: github.com/huynhtanan/google-hotels-api Setup pip install "apify-client>=3" export APIFY_TOKEN = ... # free account -> Settings -> API & Integrations 1.

articles.title: How to fix React Native build errors: Find the real error in Gradle, Xcode and metro logs
articles.excerpt: When a React Native build fails, the last line of the log ("BUILD FAILED", or a red screen on the device) almost never tells you the cause. The real error is somewhere above it, in Gradle, Xcode, Coco…
articles.body: When a React Native build fails, the last line of the log (" BUILD FAILED ", or a red screen on the device) almost never tells you the cause. The real error is somewhere above it, in Gradle, Xcode, CocoaPods, Metro or the device log. This guide covers how to find it fast, with fixes for six errors React Native developers run into all the time. For each one I'll show the raw error and what rn-build-doctor, a free, open-source CLI I built, reports for it. All the output below is real, from React Native 0.86 and 0.87 apps, an Expo SDK 57 project, Xcode 26 and an Android 14 emulator. lassiecoder / rn-build-doctor Evidence-based diagnostics for React Native and Expo build, release, and startup failures.

On Day 01 of my 30 Days of .NET challenge, we explored what happens behind a dotnet run and got to know the .NET CLI. On Day 02 , we opened up a .NET project to better understand Program.cs , .csproj , bin , obj , and some of the configurations that make our project work. So today I decided to put those two things together and take on a little challenge that reminded me of the days before AI: create, build, run, test, and publish a .NET application using only the terminal. No play button, no right-clicking the Solution, no Build menu, and no Visual Studio doing things for me. Just me, the terminal, and the .NET CLI. Just like Neo from The Matrix.

articles.title: Close the laptop, the agent keeps working
articles.excerpt: Part 2 of My Agentic Setup. Start from part 1 When an agent runs on my laptop, it stops when I close the laptop. That is fine for a five minute task. It is not fine for an audit that takes an hour, or…
articles.body: Part 2 of My Agentic Setup. Start from part 1 When an agent runs on my laptop, it stops when I close the laptop. That is fine for a five minute task. It is not fine for an audit that takes an hour, or a crew of agents working through a backlog. So my long agent work runs on a cloud VM, inside tmux. The laptop is only a window into it. The whole thing is one command: agent-session.sh my-vm --gcloud I'm on the VM. I start omp , give it work, and close the laptop. Tomorrow I run the same command, from the same laptop or the other one, and I'm back in the same place. The agent kept going while I was away. The idea is simple: the agent runs on the VM inside tmux, and the laptop is only a window, so one command starts the work or brings me back to it from any machine.

articles.title: Claude 4 Extended Reasoning: What Changes for Advanced Power Users
articles.excerpt: When I first integrated extended reasoning into a tokenization audit pipeline, the difference wasn't marginal—it was structural. The model stopped guessing and started deliberating. For those of us bu…
articles.body: When I first integrated extended reasoning into a tokenization audit pipeline, the difference wasn't marginal—it was structural. The model stopped guessing and started deliberating . For those of us building production systems in Web3 and digital forensics, that shift changes how we architect our workflows, allocate budgets, and trust automated outputs. Let me share what I've observed in practice after months of hands-on testing. From Fast Answers to Deliberate Thinking Extended reasoning in Claude 4 introduces a configurable "thinking budget"—the model can allocate thousands of tokens to internal reasoning before producing a final answer. In classic models, you got an immediate response shaped by pattern completion.

articles.title: Beat light pollution with these six portable telescopes
articles.excerpt: Sick of skyglow spoiling your stargazing? These six telescopes are portable enough that you can easily pack them away and seek out darker skies.
articles.body: Light pollution is the astronomer's biggest enemy, especially if you're gazing into deep space. And while some of the best telescopes can make a difference, there's no way to eliminate it. That's why, if you want to observe the cosmos without obstruction, you need to seek out darker skies, get a smart telescope or combine the two. You don't have to book a flight to a dark sky reserve ; just traveling away from suburbia can be enough. That's where portable telescopes come in. Set one up in a field, for example, and you'll get a vastly improved view of the cosmos. Galaxies, nebulas and other deep space objects become more detailed when they're not washed out by skyglow.

articles.title: Scientists discover 'chemical starter kit' for life in planetary birthplaces
articles.excerpt: The discovery of surprising molecules of methanol and associated maser activity has expanded the inventory of the chemical starter kit that builds planets in young star systems.
articles.body: Methanol, coming as part of the 'chemical starter kit' around young stars, has produced some unexpected surprises that could ultimately reveal some of the conditions in which planets and potentially life form around protostars. The methanol discoveries were made by astronomers using ALMA (the Atacama Large millimeter/submillimeter Array) in the Atacama Desert in Chile, as part of a project called COMPASS (the Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys). "Our work provides insight into the complex chemistry of young star systems and is ultimately an important piece of the puzzle in understanding the origin of life," said University of Bern astrophysicist Maria Drozdovskaya, who leads the COMPASS project, in a statement .

articles.body: SpaceX wants to start flying its Starship megarocket a lot more often. The company has requested permission to launch Starship from its Starbase site in South Texas up to 456 times per year. That's a big jump from the currently allowed cadence of 25. The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is in the early stages of reviewing the request. Today (Oct. 14), the agency announced "its intent to prepare a Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement, open a public scoping period and hold public scoping meetings for SpaceX’s proposal." Starship, which stands more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall, is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. It's also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX believes will revolutionize spaceflight.

articles.title: Watch SpaceX deliver more than 6,000 pounds of cargo to the ISS today
articles.excerpt: SpaceX's CRS-35 cargo Dragon will rendezvous with the International Space Station today (Oct. 15) after a two-day chase. Here's how to watch it live.
articles.body: A Dragon is closing the gap between itself and its destination after a more than two-day-long orbital pursuit. SpaceX's cargo Dragon , flying the CRS-35 (35th Commercial Resupply Services) mission for NASA , is scheduled to rendezvous with the International Space Station (ISS) this morning (Oct. 15), delivering fresh food, long-term provisions, research and hardware to the orbital lab and its crew. Coverage of Dragon's arrival at the ISS will begin at 9:15 a.m. EDT (1315 GMT), with docking scheduled for approximately 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT). A livestream of the rendezvous will be available here and on Space.com's homepage, courtesy of NASA. SpaceX's CRS-35 launch creates a "space jellyfish" in the sky on Oct. 13.

articles.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
articles.excerpt: "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
articles.body: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet of Things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered.
